verdict: Airbnb grew revenue 17% to $3.6B as nights and seats booked rose 10%, and net income jumped to $816M — helped by higher operating profit and a $77M tax benefit tied to prior-year taxes.

segments.name: Stays & experiences
segments.note: Service fees on every stay, experience and service booked. Airbnb reports a single revenue stream; the bookings behind it were worth $27.2B in gross booking value.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Supporting hosts and guests — customer service, trust & safety and host insurance.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Building the app and new products like experiences and services.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Marketing to win travelers and hosts.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Bookings value accelerated
takeaways.text: Gross booking value rose 16% to $27.2B on 10% more nights and seats booked and a moderate rise in nightly rates — growth accelerated in core markets like the U.S., France, the UK and Australia.

takeaways.title: Profit jumped on two boosts
takeaways.text: Net income rose from $642M to $816M (a 23% margin). Higher operating income did most of the work, and a $77M benefit related to prior-year taxes — from newly published guidance — helped too.

takeaways.title: A third of revenue became free cash
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $1.3B, 35% of revenue, and $4.8B over the last twelve months — guests pay upfront, hosts are paid after check-in.

oneTimers: The tax line includes a $77M benefit recorded in the quarter related to recently published guidance impacting prior-year taxes; without it, the tax bill would have been higher and net income lower.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$139M: $183M of interest earned (Airbnb holds billions in guest payments before stays happen), minus $37M of interest expense and $7M of other expense.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
